heading.__example__: C1 · Quality of Questions Asked by the Teacher

definition.__example__: What kinds of questions the teacher asks, and whether they make children think. A closed question needs a yes/no or one-word answer, an open question needs a longer answer, and the strongest questions ask "why" and are followed up.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: No questions asked by the teacher, or asks the questions but gives the answers without waiting for students to answer.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: Teacher only asks closed questions with yes/no or one word answers.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: Teacher asks at least two open questions and waits for students to answer.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Teacher asks at least one question using 'why' and then follows up on the same child's answer (why? how do you know?).

heading.__example__: C2 · Helping when a child is wrong

definition.__example__: What the teacher does when a child's answer is wrong or incomplete: ignores it, says it is wrong, explains why, or helps the child fix it. It only applies when an answer was actually wrong.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: A student gives a wrong answer and the teacher ignores it, or only repeats the same explanation in the same words.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: The teacher says the answer is wrong, or explains again, but gives the reason for the correction at most once.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: At least two times, the teacher gives the reason for the correction and says what was right and what to change.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher asks the student or another student to fix the answer, and tries a new way (a new example, a picture, smaller steps) if they are still stuck.

definition.__example__: How the teacher chooses who answers: only children who put a hand up or call out, or ways of bringing in other children, such as calling different children by name, pair talk, or everyone writing an answer.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: The teacher asks the whole class and takes whoever answers. No way of choosing who answers is heard: no name called before the question, no talking in pairs, no "everyone write".

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: The teacher uses a way of choosing who answers one time, for example calls a student by name, then goes back to taking whoever answers.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: At least two times, the teacher uses a way of choosing who answers (a name called before the question, "tell your partner", "everyone write your answer", names picked at random).

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher calls at least two different names to answer, and each is followed by an answer.

coach_adds.__example__: Coach adds: choosing that cannot be heard (pointing, a nod, "you tell" with no name), and whether children who had not put a hand up were brought in. The coach sets the final level with a written justification.

definition.__example__: Whether children have a say in how the lesson goes: a real choice about how to do the work or explain it, the teacher taking up a child's idea, or a part of the lesson handed to them. Small choices (who goes first, which colour) are not real choices.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: The teacher decides everything and asks students for no choice or idea.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: The teacher lets students choose only small things (who goes first, which colour), and decides everything about the learning.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: The teacher gives students at least one real choice about how to do the work or how to explain it, and lets them follow it, or takes up a child's idea.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher hands a part of the lesson to students: a student or a group leads an activity, picks the method, or teaches the others.

definition.__example__: How smoothly the class moves from one activity to the next: whether the teacher gives a clear signal and how long the change takes.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: The class takes more than three minutes to change activity, and the teacher gives no clear signal.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: The teacher gives a signal, but the change still takes two to three minutes.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: The class changes activity in under two minutes of the teacher's signal.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, students already know what comes next and change without being told.

coach_adds.__example__: Coach adds: how long the class actually took to settle into the next activity (chairs moved, books out, working), which the transcript times only roughly. The coach sets the final level with a written justification.

definition.__example__: Whether children feel safe to try and be wrong: how the teacher responds to their answers, whether praise is for effort or only for right answers, and whether mistakes are treated as useful.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: The teacher gives no encouragement. Replies to students are flat, dismissive, or only about the task.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: The teacher praises, but only for right answers or for doing as told, and only in general words.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: At least two times, the teacher praises a student's effort, trying, or thinking, not just a right answer.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher treats a wrong answer or an attempt as useful, and also invites other views.

definition.__example__: Whether the teacher sets real pair or group work: a task the group can only finish together, with something to make, roles and a report back. Sitting together but working alone is not group work.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: The teacher gives no pair or group task. Everyone works alone or as one class.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: The teacher puts students in pairs or groups, but each student does their own work.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: The teacher gives a task that a group can only finish together, and says what the group must make.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher gives roles or turns inside the group, and asks the group to report back.

coach_adds.__example__: Coach adds: whether the groups actually worked together on one product and used the roles, which is mostly silent or too quiet for the recording. The coach sets the final level with a written justification.

definition.__example__: Whether books, the board, charts or objects are used for learning, and by whom: only shown by the teacher, used by the children, or used by a child to explain while the teacher builds on what the child says.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: The teacher never mentions a book, the board, a chart, or any object or picture.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: The teacher mentions a book, the board, or an object only to show or tell, and does not ask students to use it.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: The teacher asks students to use a book, the board, or an object themselves, and says how it connects to the idea.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher asks a student to explain with the book, the chart or the object, and builds on what the student says.

definition.__example__: How deep children's answers are: one word, a longer answer that only repeats what was said, or an answer that shows reasoning in the child's own words (says why, compares, uses a rule on a new case, explains a choice, gives their own example).

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: Students give only one-word answers or repeat a fact.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: At least one answer, from any student, is longer than a phrase, but it only repeats what was already said or read, or finishes the teacher's sentence.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: At least two answers, from any students, show reasoning in the child's own words: they say why, compare two things, use a rule on a new case, or explain a choice. Finishing the teacher's sentence, or repeating a reason the teacher already gave, does not count.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, a student gives their own example, or links the idea to something else, that the teacher did not say first.

definition.__example__: How many different children speak across the lesson, and whether children silent early on speak later.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: No student speaks during the lesson.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: Only the same one or two children speak.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: Three to five different children speak.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Six or more different children speak, and at least two children who had not spoken in the first half speak in the second half.

coach_adds.__example__: Coach adds: how many different children spoke, and how many children who were quiet in the first half spoke in the second. The coach sets the final level with a written justification.

help_why.__example__: At least 20 characters: what you saw in the room.

definition.__example__: Whether children talk to each other about the task, not only to the teacher: one child answers, agrees with or adds to what another said. At its strongest they give reasons to agree or disagree and reach one shared answer.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: No student speaks to another student about the task.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: One time, a student answers and the teacher names a second child who agrees with the previous student's answer, or the student says I agree with her/him referring to the previously given answer by the student.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: At least two times, a student answers, agrees with, or adds to what another student just said.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, students give a reason to agree or disagree with each other, and reach one shared answer.

coach_adds.__example__: Coach adds: children talking to each other about the task that the recording did not pick up, mostly during pair and group work, and whether they gave reasons or reached a shared answer. The coach sets the final level with a written justification.

help_why.__example__: At least 20 characters: what you saw in the room.

definition.__example__: Whether children dare to answer when they are not sure: they stay silent, answer only when sure, answer while unsure, or answer unasked and try again after a wrong answer. Only the trying counts, not whether the answer is right.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: When the teacher asks, students stay silent, say "I do not know", or wait for the teacher to give the answer.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: Students answer only when they are sure. Nobody gives a half-sure answer; when unsure they say nothing.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: At least two times, a student answers while clearly unsure, for example "Maybe...", "Should I say...?", or an answer that changes halfway.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, a student answers without being asked, or tries again after a wrong answer instead of giving up.

coach_adds.__example__: Coach adds: how children behave when they are unsure: whether they have a go or go quiet, put a hand up or wait for the teacher, and try again after a wrong answer. The coach sets the final level with a written justification.

help_why.__example__: At least 20 characters: what you saw in the room.

definition.__example__: Whether children ask questions of their own: only about the task (which page, may I answer), or about the idea itself (how or why something works, a different case). Repeating the teacher's question or giving an unsure answer does not count.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: No student asks the teacher a question of their own. An unsure answer ("Is it twelve?") or a student repeating the teacher's question ("Why?") does not count.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: Students ask only questions about the task: which page, do we write this, is it homework, may I answer, or please say it again.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: Students ask at least one question about the idea itself: how or why something works, or what would happen in a different case.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, students ask at least two questions about the idea, and one of them is about something the teacher has not talked about in this lesson.

definition.__example__: Whether what the teacher says about the subject is correct, and whether a wrong statement is corrected. Count something as wrong only when you are sure.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: The teacher says something wrong and leaves it, so students are left with wrong information. Count something as wrong only if you are sure; a word that may be a transcription or translation mistake does not count.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: Mostly correct, but the teacher makes a small slip (a wrong rule or a wrong word) and does not correct it.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: Everything the teacher says is correct. When not sure, the teacher says so and does not guess.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher warns students about a common mistake before they make it.

definition.__example__: Whether the teacher uses the subject's own words (such as "numerator" or "verb") and explains them, and whether children are made to use them.

__example__.title: Developing

__example__.title: Proficient

__example__.title: Highly Effective

definition.__example__: Whether the teacher explains why a rule or step works, with a reason, an example or a picture, or only says how to do it. At its strongest, the teacher turns a child's question into a short lesson or asks the children to give the reason.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: The teacher only says how to do it, and gives no reason.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: The teacher gives a reason now and then, but mostly asks students to remember the rule.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: At least two times, the teacher explains why a rule or step works, with a reason, an example, or a picture.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher turns a student's question into a short lesson that goes further, or asks the children to give the reason.

definition.__example__: Whether the teacher links the lesson to real life, another subject or an earlier lesson, with an example or comparison, and explains the link. At its strongest, children build on the teacher's link.

err_note.__example__:
Please fix these before you go on:
• Choose a level.

__example__.title: Not Observed
__example__.description: The teacher gives no real-life example, comparison, or link to another subject or an earlier lesson.

__example__.title: Developing
__example__.description: The teacher mentions a link and moves on without explaining it.

__example__.title: Proficient
__example__.description: The teacher gives a link and explains how it fits the idea.

__example__.title: Highly Effective
__example__.description: Beyond level 3, a student builds on the teacher's link: they add to it, ask about it, or explain it in their own words.
